questions.scenario: The meta-rule for handling ANY exception is:
options: Skip documents — emergencies excuse paperwork
Normal accounting rules + EXTRA evidence chain + explicit approval + named owner with deadline
Wait for year-end and fix everything then
Let each department improvise freely
questions.explanation: Exceptions change EVENTS, never RULES. More chaos = more documentation per event, an accountable owner, and a clock. Undocumented recoveries become unexplainable balances.
wrongExplanations: The Golden Rule holds hardest on bad Thursdays.
Year-end archaeology is how mysteries are manufactured.
Improvisation without structure is where honest factories grow ghosts.

questions.scenario: H&M's valid claim settles at ৳15L credit, goods NOT returned. Correct entry:
options: Dr Inventory / Cr COGS
Dr Sales Returns & Claims 15L / Cr AR—H&M 15L via approved credit note
Dr Cash / Cr Revenue
No entry — just remember it for next invoice
questions.explanation: A price-reduction claim reverses part of the ORIGINAL revenue event through a contra-revenue account and reduces the buyer's receivable — documented by claim file + settlement approval + credit note.
wrongExplanations: Nothing came back, so inventory/COGS don't move.
Masco RECEIVES nothing here — it forgoes collection of 15L.
Silent next-invoice adjustments break both matching and buyer reconciliation (this module's shortcut trap).

questions.scenario: LC discrepancy: invoice says 100% cotton, certificate says 98%. Bank refuses payment. Accounting impact TODAY:
options: Reverse the sale immediately
Write off the receivable
NO new journal entry — the money entries were correct; this is a DOCUMENT problem threatening cash timing (aging keeps running!)
Reduce revenue by 2%
questions.explanation: Revenue was recognized on B/L date correctly; the discrepancy blocks COLLECTION, not recognition. Cure = corrected/waived DOCUMENTS, chased urgently because realization windows don't pause.
wrongExplanations: The shipment happened; ownership passed; reversing would falsify history.
A curable document mismatch isn't uncollectability.
The cotton difference is between DOCUMENTS, not necessarily price.

questions.scenario: Dead pump: emergency repair ৳22L, routine restoration only. Where does it go?
options: Capitalize into the machine's cost
Dr Repairs & Maintenance (factory OH) / Cr Bank or AP — expense as period overhead
Charge to H&M's account
Spread secretly across garment orders
questions.explanation: Module 10's test: restoration WITHOUT life extension = period repair cost into factory OH. Capitalization is reserved for overhauls ADDING future benefit.
wrongExplanations: Only life/capacity-extending work gets capitalized.
Buyers pay for garments, not our maintenance.
Hidden spreading corrupts every order's costing (Module 5).

questions.scenario: 'Just reduce their NEXT invoice quietly instead of a credit note.' Two failures of this shortcut:
options: It's slower and uses more paper
Breaks document traceability AND misstates two periods' revenue/matching; also destroys claim statistics
Nothing wrong — accounting accepts it
Credit notes require bank permission
questions.explanation: Invisible deductions make Masco-vs-buyer reconciliation archaeology; costs land in months that didn't earn them; defect patterns vanish from management view. Credit notes exist precisely to keep claims honest.
wrongExplanations: Backwards — shortcuts CREATE future investigation work.
This exact pattern is what audits flag and Module 12 prevents.
Credit notes are internal commercial documents — no bank involved.

questions.scenario: Insurance will likely cover ৳20L of the pump disaster. Recording order:
options: Ignore the loss, show only net ৳2L
Record full loss/costs when incurred; record insurance RECOVERY separately when confirmed (gross honesty)
Wait until insurance pays before recording anything
Book recovery as revenue
questions.explanation: Books tell the whole story: damage happened (expense), reimbursement expected (separate asset/recovery line when probable). Net presentation hides both the risk event and the protection working.
wrongExplanations: Netting hides operational problems management must see.
Deferring reality until cash arrives violates accrual — again.
Insurance recovery compensates a loss; it isn't earned income.

options: Nobody — exceptions handle themselves
Commercial: claims & LC discrepancies. Production/engineering: breakdowns. Finance: ledger truth + open-exception register review weekly
Only the MD may touch exceptions
Whichever intern is free
questions.explanation: Ownership plus deadlines plus weekly aged-review (Module 9's ladder applied to exceptions) keeps resolutions moving. Unowned exceptions rot into audit findings.
wrongExplanations: Exceptions demand MORE ownership than routine events.
Escalation exists, but daily handling is distributed by nature.
Interns learn on shadows of exceptions, not the real ones.

questions.scenario: QC confirms Line 3 caused the defect claim. Beyond the credit note, what SHOULD follow?
options: Blame and terminate the line operators immediately
Root-cause corrective action + monthly defect-rate tracking per line — claims data feeding process improvement (and future costing/pricing decisions)
Stop recording claims so metrics look better
Switch all production to Line 4 forever
questions.explanation: Claims are expensive feedback. Documented root cause + tracked defect rates turn losses into prevention — and give merchandising honest quality data for future negotiations.
wrongExplanations: Punishment-first cultures hide defects NEXT time — worse outcomes.
Hiding metrics guarantees repeat claims at compound prices.
Capacity decisions need analysis, not panic.

questions.scenario: Buyer returns 300 defective pcs physically. Warehouse receives them. Proper flow:
options: Throw them away quietly
GRN-reversal style entry WITH QC tagging: inventory increases at scrap/rework value, AR adjusted per settlement, damage classification documented
Add them back as first-quality sellable stock
Count them in next month's production output
questions.explanation: Physical returns need document-backed flows exactly like receipts (Golden Rule). Their VALUE depends on disposition: reworkable vs scrap — decided by QC and recorded accordingly.
wrongExplanations: Undocumented disposal destroys both assets and evidence.
Known-defective units as first quality re-sells the same claim to the next shipment.
Production output records NEW manufacture; returns are reverse-logistics.

questions.scenario: Rafiq designs the exceptions module. The most valuable single feature:
options: Auto-approve small credits under ৳10k
An open-exceptions register: every claim/discrepancy/breakdown with owner, age, next action, deadline — reviewed weekly, escalated automatically at thresholds
Hide exceptions from dashboards to avoid panic
Allow deleting resolved exceptions to keep lists clean
questions.explanation: Visibility with accountability IS exception management. Auto-approvals recreate Module 12's toxic shortcuts; hidden lists rot; deletion destroys learning trails.
wrongExplanations: Small auto-credits aggregate into big silent leaks — Module 12 said no.
Panic is cured by process, not blindness.
Resolved exceptions are history teachers — archived, never deleted.
